description:
FILED s470bt (Opus, 2026-09-06) by the B6 IR conformance corpus (5 cases).
Three separate bugs; split when scheduled.

PROBES (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL main cd34df72):

(a) modulus with an infinite operand
      no warnings 'numeric'; my $inf = 9**9**9;
      print "5%inf=", 5 % $inf, " -5%inf=", -5 % $inf, " 5%-inf=", 5 % -$inf, "\n";
    perl  5%inf=5 -5%inf=Inf 5%-inf=-Inf
    PCL   5%inf=NaN -5%inf=NaN 5%-inf=NaN
    -- perl's integer modulus with a right operand it cannot fit falls back to
    the floating rule (result has the RIGHT operand's sign); PCL produces NaN
    for every combination.

(b) an integer-valued double at or above 2**53 stringifies exactly
      my @n = (2**63, 2**64);  print join(",", @n), "\n";
    perl  9.22337203685478e+18,1.84467440737096e+19
    PCL   9223372036854775808,18446744073709551616
    -- `**` returns an NV in perl, so it prints through %.15g.  PCL's `**`
    returns an exact integer, which then prints all its digits.  (A literal
    "9223372036854775808" converted with 0+ agrees in both.)

(c) Internals::SvREADONLY on an array
      my @a=(1,2); print "A", scalar(@a), "\n";
      Internals::SvREADONLY(@a,1); print "B", scalar(@a), "\n";
    perl  A2 / B2        PCL  A2 / B12
    -- after the call, `scalar(@a)` yields the array's ELEMENTS (1,2 printed
    as "12") instead of the count.  The read-only part works: a later `push`
    dies in both.

CORPUS CASES: 251-regex 252-regex (a) 276-sort (b) 010-array 245-regex (c).

=== DONE (s473d) === -- all three parts, one per commit

  (a) `%` with an infinite operand      SHIPPED, s473d member 2 = task #1191.
      pp_modulo's two regimes arm for arm; `5 % inf` is 5, `-5 % inf` is Inf,
      `5 % -inf` is -Inf, and only a NaN operand gives NaN.  ir-conform
      251-numeric + 252-numeric left known-fail.tsv BY EDIT.  ir-spec 3.5.

  (b) `**` returns an NV                SHIPPED, s473d member 3.
      pp_pow's branch rule implemented: a POWER-OF-TWO base by repeated
      squaring in DOUBLES (so 2**52 prints 4.5035996273705e+15), any other
      base in integers only while exponent*bitlength(base) <= 64, everything
      else C's pow().  THE MEASUREMENT THAT MATTERS: perl returns an NV for
      results that fit an IV comfortably, so this was NEVER the 64-bit
      boundary and needed no IV/UV distinction.  Two IEEE edges came with it
      ((-8)**(1/3) leaked a CL COMPLEX; 0**-1 died with SBCL's
      division-by-zero where C's pow is +Inf).  cl/pack-impl.pl depended on
      the old exactness -- both `2 ** N` sites became repeated multiplication,
      cl/pcl-pack.lisp regenerated, perl-tests/pack.t 5636/89 = baseline.
      ir-conform 276-numeric left known-fail.tsv BY EDIT.  ir-spec 3.6.

  (c) Internals::SvREADONLY(@a,1) and scalar(@a)   SHIPPED, s473d member 5.
      The read-only storage was a plain SIMPLE vector, and that answered NO to
      TWO different questions: ARRAY-HAS-FILL-POINTER-P is the WRITABILITY
      test (that part worked), but ADJUSTABLE-ARRAY-P is the "is this value an
      array variable's STORAGE" test that SIXTEEN sites ask -- so a read-only
      array stopped being an array for all of them.  Measured family:
      `scalar(@a)`, `0+@a`, `my $n = @a`, `$n = @a`, `scalar(@$r)`, `0+@$r`,
      `sub { @a }->()` and `sprintf "%s", scalar(@a)` (which even warned
      "Redundant argument", the vector flattening into two arguments); `$#a`,
      the boolean test, "@a", join, foreach, grep, map, sort, slices, keys and
      element reads were already right, which is why only SCALAR context was
      broken.

      THE FIX IS THE STORAGE, not sixteen predicates: read-only storage is now
      an ADJUSTABLE vector with NO FILL POINTER.  Widening the predicates was
      the wrong shape -- nothing structural distinguishes a read-only array
      from a `p-..` range temp, so a widened predicate would have started
      collapsing LIST temporaries to their length.  One belt:
      %p-array-grow-discarding now asks for the fill pointer too (ADJUST-ARRAY
      would otherwise silently resize a read-only array; unreachable today,
      every caller is behind %p-check-array-writable).  ir-conform 010-array +
      245-array left known-fail.tsv BY EDIT.  ir-spec 2.3's read-only-array
      paragraph rewritten with the two questions in a table.

      FILED FROM ITS PROBES: #1370 -- `"n=" . @a` gives n=ARRAY(0x1) where perl
      gives n=3, and `@a eq "3"` is false.  A DIFFERENT mechanism (an array in
      scalar context collapses to its count for NUMBERS but not for STRINGS)
      that diverges for an ordinary WRITABLE array too, so it is pre-existing
      and not part of this family.

BARS on the final s473d tree (all five members): gate 223 files / 7707 rows,
only the 13 pclxs xs rows; full sweep GATE clean, 0 new / 0 fixed / 0 LOST,
TOTAL passing 18674 (+0), drops census 5 = current 5, pack.t 5636/89;
corpus-diff emission IDENTICAL over 111 files + 6 shapes (runtime-only, NO
generation bump); emission-ab over lib SAME=27 DIFF=0 RCDIFF=0; ir-conform 301
pass / 0 fail / 44 known / 0 stale; ir-host-leak byte-identical to the base
extraction's report (31 leaks, unchanged); companion --jobs 1 over op/sprintf.t
op/sprintf2.t op/numconvert.t op/inf_nan.t op/pow.t op/int.t op/array.t, BEFORE
(a c4304834 extraction) and AFTER, identical file for file and equal to the
baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv snapshot -- 0 movers, nothing spliced.
subject: THREE numeric/array divergences found by the ir-conform corpus: `%` with an Inf operand answers NaN, 2**63 stringifies as an exact integer where perl prints %.15g, and `Internals::SvREADONLY(@a,1)` leaves scalar(@a) returning the ELEMENTS
